business_problem: Royal London Group needed to review thousands of regulated marketing assets faster while maintaining compliance with FCA Consumer Duty requirements and reducing the burden on human reviewers.
solution_summary: Cognizant and Royal London Group implemented a governed generative AI review assistant to shorten the compliance cycle for regulated marketing content. The solution uses Microsoft Azure’s OpenAI LLM inside a modular assistant split into three personas—Creator, Refiner and Approver—so content generation, improvement and approval follow explicit stages instead of a single opaque model call. That persona-based architecture mirrors Royal London Group’s existing content workflow and makes outputs easier to audit. Each asset moves through the assistant under human-in-the-loop controls, with subject matter experts performing the final review before anything is approved. Cognizant also refined the assistant through stakeholder feedback, quality assurance checks and scaled evaluation, while embedding generative AI skills inside Royal London teams so the process can be reused economically in a highly regulated environment.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Azure’s OpenAI LLM
solution_components.role: Provides the foundation model used to analyze and rewrite regulated marketing content.

solution_components.name: Creator
solution_components.role: Handles the content-creation stage inside the assistant’s governed workflow.

solution_components.name: Refiner
solution_components.role: Improves draft content before approval so quality and compliance feedback can be applied in sequence.

solution_components.name: Approver
solution_components.role: Checks content in the approval stage so outputs align with governance expectations before human signoff.

solution_components.name: final SME review
solution_components.role: Keeps human subject matter experts in the loop for the last compliance decision on each asset.

data_flow: Regulated marketing assets enter the modular assistant, where the Creator, Refiner and Approver personas apply staged Azure OpenAI processing rather than a single model pass. Outputs are then checked by human subject matter experts in the final SME review, and the assistant is continuously refined through stakeholder feedback, QA checks and scaled evaluation.
business_outcome: Royal London Group reduced the time spent reviewing regulated marketing assets, eased manual reviewer workload and established a scalable, auditable model for using generative AI in a regulated content process.
metrics: 4.2 hours reduced per asset review time
architecture_clues: The assistant uses three personas to mirror Royal London Group’s traditional content workflow.
Human oversight remained central, with every AI-generated output undergoing final SME review.
Quality assurance checks and scaled evaluation were part of the refinement loop before reuse at scale.
The implementation focused on transparency and auditability for a regulated insurer.
